voiceover:
[conversational] This free tool turns one topic into a finished video, but there's a catch.

Stay till the end, because one catch can stop you on step one.

It's called MoneyPrinterTurbo. Look at the GitHub page: over 100k stars. Type a topic, and it writes the script, adds voice-over, subtitles and music, and pulls stock footage.

The code's free. But it's not zero cost. You need an LLM, and a local Ollama model works, plus a stock-footage key. And it runs on your computer, not your phone.

[serious] The honest catch: the footage is generic stock, so it can look like every other faceless video. No avatars, no real editor.

Worth it for tinkerers making high-volume faceless clips. Skip it for brand-building.

[whispers] Here's the catch I promised: Pexels has paused new API keys, and old tutorials still tell you to get one. Use Pixabay or Coverr, or your own clips.

[curious] Would you put stock footage on your brand? Send this to the friend who pays monthly for video tools. Hack saved?

title: FREE AI VIDEO MAKER
ig_caption:
This free tool turns one topic into a finished video, but there's a catch.
✅ The code is free and open-source, but you run it on your own computer
✅ You need an LLM (a local Ollama model works) and a stock-footage key
✅ Pexels paused new API keys, so use Pixabay or Coverr, or your own clips
✅ Great for high-volume faceless clips, weak for brand-building
Would you put generic stock footage on your brand? Tell me below 👇

topic: Review of MoneyPrinterTurbo, a free open-source tool that turns one topic into a finished video (script, voice-over, stock footage, subtitles, music), and whether it's worth using for business content

pick.topic: Review of MoneyPrinterTurbo, a free open-source tool that turns one topic into a finished video (script, voice-over, stock footage, subtitles, music), and whether it's worth using for business content
pick.angle: Stop paying monthly for AI video tools: this free one makes a full video from one topic. Here's the catch before you build your brand on it.
pick.why: 63k views and 3,756 likes on an 84s reel, a strong like rate. It's a free alternative to paid AI video tools, which fits our review slot and builds on the Higgsfield 'free alternative' angle without repeating it. The GitHub page and demo can be shown live. The honest catch is setup effort, API keys, generic stock footage and platforms demoting mass-produced content.

research.availability: The code is free (MIT) and self-hosted on Windows, macOS or Linux. It is not a phone app or a hosted service. You still need an LLM (a free local Ollama model or a paid API key) and a stock-footage key. Pexels has paused NEW API keys, so use Pixabay or Coverr for new setups.
steps: Pick an install path. Windows one-click: download the .7z from the latest GitHub release. Docker: clone the repo, then run `docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d`. Python: `python -m pip install mpt` (the official PyPI package is 'mpt'; the PyPI package named 'MoneyPrinterTurbo' is third-party).

Source install needs Python 3.11 or later: `git clone https://github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.git`, `cd MoneyPrinterTurbo`, `uv python install 3.11`, `uv sync --frozen`. Start the WebUI with `sh webui.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `.\webui.bat` (Windows).
Open the WebUI at http://127.0.0.1:8501 (Docker or local).
Expand 'Basic Settings' and enter at least one LLM provider key and one video-source key (Pixabay or Coverr; Pexels only if you already hold a key). A local Ollama model can replace a paid LLM key.
Under 'Video Script Settings', type the Video Subject (the topic) and choose Script Language. Optionally click 'Generate Video Script and Keywords' to have the LLM write the script.
Under Video Settings choose Video Source and aspect ratio (9:16 for Reels). Under Audio Settings choose the voice and Background Music. Under Subtitle Settings choose font and position.
Click 'Generate Video', wait for processing, preview the result, then click 'Download Video'.
facts: The project's GitHub description: provide a topic or keyword, and it generates the script, matches footage, creates subtitles and background music, and renders an HD short video. (github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo README-en)
It runs through the WebUI, API, CLI or an AI agent workflow (README-en).
The repo is hugely popular. The config.example.toml page shows Star 126k and Fork 19.5k (GitHub, fetched snapshot).

Verdent describes it as an MIT-licensed Python project that chains an LLM, stock-media APIs like Pexels, text-to-speech and video tooling (MoviePy, FFmpeg) into one pipeline driven by a Streamlit web UI or REST API.
The default pipeline only costs LLM tokens. Edge TTS and Pexels are free; AI-video sources bill per second of footage (terminalskills.io skill page).
A fully free path exists: Ollama for the script, Edge TTS for voice-over (no key), and a free Pexels or Pixabay key for footage (localaimaster.com).
The repo's v1.3.0 release added Coverr as a stock-video provider and Groq as an LLM provider. video_source accepts pexels, pixabay, coverr or local (your own clips).
Requirements: Python 3.11 (3.11 recommended), FFmpeg, at least 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended) and at least one LLM provider key (riffkit.ai guide).
Subtitles: the subtitle provider can be 'edge' (fast) or 'whisper' (higher quality, GPU-accelerated). Default font is MicrosoftYaHeiBold.ttc and default position is bottom (pyshine.com, deepwiki).

Newer releases added word-by-word subtitles with a pop-up spring animation, reusable settings presets with import/export, and a redesigned WebUI with a settings dialog and improved dark mode (GitHub Releases page).
Output files per task include the final video, audio.mp3 and a subtitle .srt (deepwiki quick start).

Pexels API: 'New API key issuance is currently paused and cannot be requested.' (pexels.com/api, since about 30 Sept 2026). Rate-limit increases are also paused. Keys already issued keep the default 200 requests/hour and 20,000/month (help.pexels.com).

Pexels content is free to use commercially under the Pexels License. The API guidelines ask for a prominent link to Pexels and photographer credit where possible (pexels.com/api/documentation, agentgid summary).
Pixabay API still issues keys instantly; one comparison lists its limit as 100 requests/minute (pexafy.com comparison, checked 14 Oct 2026).
The official repo offers a free 'Open in Colab' notebook and a prebuilt Docker image: ghcr.io/harry0703/moneyprinterturbo:latest.
do_not_claim: Do NOT say it needs zero accounts, zero keys or zero setup. It needs an LLM and a stock-footage key (or local footage), plus a Python/Docker install.
Do NOT say 'just get a free Pexels key'. Pexels is not issuing new keys, so a new viewer can't follow that step.
Do NOT say it works on a phone or in a browser tab. You run it on your own computer (a third-party hosted site, moneyprinterturbo.app, exists but is not the official project).
Do NOT say it is 'completely free forever'. The code is free, but LLM APIs, AI-video sources and paid TTS can cost money.
Do NOT claim it makes you money or that the output is 'ready to go viral'. 'Money' is only in the name. No source supports earnings claims.
Do NOT call the stock clips exclusive or original. They are generic stock footage that other users can pull from the same libraries.
Do NOT tell people to pip install 'MoneyPrinterTurbo'. That PyPI package is third-party; the official one is 'mpt'.
The reel's caption has no verifiable claims beyond the repo's own description. The transcript was unavailable, so nothing else was checked.

Do NOT say it is a plug-and-play replacement for CapCut, HeyGen or similar paid tools. It does not make avatars or talking-head video and has no real video editor in the WebUI. The local video project workflow is CLI-only (GitHub Releases).
criticism: Setup is technical: Python 3.11, FFmpeg, Docker or a Windows package, plus API keys. Non-technical business owners may get stuck (riffkit.ai, codersera guides).

The stock-footage key bottleneck is real. Pexels has paused new API keys, and a missing or wrong footage key is the usual cause when generation hangs at 'Searching materials' (pexels.com/api, codersera).

Stock-footage matching is keyword-based, so clips can feel generic or off-topic. For a brand this makes videos look like every other faceless stock video. This is a judgement; the sources only describe the keyword matching.
Free is not entirely free: the script needs an LLM key (or local Ollama on your own hardware), and AI-video sources bill per second of footage (terminalskills.io, agentpedia).
Licence and rule checking is on you: Pexels asks for credit/links under its API terms, and one guide says to check Pexels, Pixabay, music, likeness and trademark rules (agentpedia.codes).

Security default: config.example.toml sets listen_host to 0.0.0.0 and the API has no authentication unless an API key is set. On a shared network, set listen_host to 127.0.0.1 or set an API key (mrtechking.com scan, terminalskills.io).
The README is crowded with sponsor and referral blocks for model-API resellers (mrtechking.com scan).

Open-source dependency: the project is maintained by one main developer, and menus and providers change between releases (v1.3.x added new providers and a WebUI redesign). Re-check the steps before filming.

ui.platforms: Web UI in a desktop browser (Streamlit app on localhost:8501), run on Windows, macOS or Linux. No iOS or Android app.
apps: Terminal / Command Prompt or Docker Desktop (install)
Pixabay or Pexels API page (get the footage key)
screens: GitHub repo page: title 'MoneyPrinterTurbo 💸', the Chinese/English tagline about generating HD short videos from a topic or keyword, and the star count near the top right (about 126k at the last snapshot).
README-en: the 'Installation & Deployment 📥' section, with the 'Download the latest Windows one-click package' link and the Docker command `docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d`.
Terminal: the commands above running. After start-up the browser opens at localhost:8501.

WebUI page: the browser tab title is 'MoneyPrinterTurbo'. A collapsible 'Basic Settings' area sits near the top for LLM provider, API keys and video-source keys. The newer release has a dedicated settings dialog. Streamlit headers are hidden by custom CSS.

Main form in three columns, per the older layout, so check the current version: LEFT 'Video Script Settings' (Video Subject text box, Script Language, button 'Generate Video Script and Keywords', script and keyword boxes). MIDDLE 'Video Settings' (Video Source, Video Concat Mode, aspect ratio, clip duration, Number of Videos) and 'Audio Settings' (voice, Speech Volume, Background Music, music volume). RIGHT 'Subtitle Settings' (Enable Subtitles, Font, Position, colour, size).
Bottom of the form: the 'Generate Video' button. A log or progress area follows while it renders.

Result: a video player preview showing the finished vertical video with burned-in subtitles at the bottom, plus a 'Download Video' button. The default theme follows Streamlit (typically light); the newer release adds improved dark-mode support. Check which theme you get on your machine.

research.visuals: Show the GitHub repo page (stars, tagline), then a real screen recording of the WebUI: type a topic, click 'Generate Video', and play the finished vertical video with subtitles. Only a real screen recording can prove the output quality, so use it to show the generic stock-clip look honestly. Then show the Pexels API page with the 'paused' notice as the catch.

research.notes: Angle is OK with a fix: lead with 'free software, but not zero-cost or zero-effort'. The most current catch is that Pexels paused new API keys around 30 Sept 2026, and many older tutorials and the popular reel's ecosystem still say 'get a free Pexels key'. Tell viewers to use Pixabay or Coverr, or their own local clips. This is a self-hosted tool, so the honest verdict is: great for tinkerers and for high-volume faceless clips, weak for brand-building because of generic stock footage and technical setup. The WebUI was redesigned in a recent release (settings dialog, dark mode), so the three-column layout and labels from older guides may differ; screen-record the live version before recreating it. GitHub star and fork counts vary by snapshot (102k, 119k, 126k seen), so say 'over 100k stars' or check live. The reel's caption (Indonesian) matches the project description and is not wrong, just incomplete: it omits the keys and setup requirements.
